lina (devex): Heads-up: weird auth behavior hit during onboarding workshop. The auto-rotate tool replaced my project token with an org-scoped key and the sampleapp started calling the wrong workspace.

rafa (sdk): whoa. auto-rotate did what now?

lina (devex): Repro steps: set REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=proj_abc, run `rw-rotate --auto` (local), afterwards `REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY` in my env was unchanged but the keyring entry referenced `rw:latest` and returned org_key_xyz instead. sampleapp then billed org account.

priya (platform): we had a rotate job that writes back to the keyring when keys are refreshed. Looks like the writer uses a non-namespaced key id `redwood:token` which would clobber whichever token was there.

oliver (security): can you paste the keyring patch? this sounds like an elevation/overwriting risk.

lina (devex): snippet from rotate helper: `keyring.set('redwood:token', newKey)` and loader: `keyring.get('redwood:token') || process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_ORG_KEY`

rafa (sdk): oh wow. two problems: (1) keyring uses a single global key id, (2) loader checks keyring before env vars so container images can silently pick up rotated org keys.

priya (platform): agreed. Proposed fixes: (A) namespaced key ids `redwood:project:<id>:token` and `redwood:org:<id>:token`, (B) loader precedence should prefer explicit env vars first, then keyring, (C) rotate should write back to the exact namespaced key.

oliver (security): strongly +1. Also add an audit log entry on rotate operations and a confirmation prompt when rotating in interactive mode: "You're rotating an org-scoped key. This will affect other projects. Proceed? (y/N)"

rafa (sdk): I'll open a small PR to flip the loader order and add namespacing. Also adding unit tests for these env combinations: only env, only keyring, both env+keyring (org vs project), and rotate write behavior.

lina (devex): can we also add a runtime detection warning: if keyring token scope != current project meta, print `WARNING: keyring token scope mismatch (using org token for project). See <link>`? New devs waste hours on this.

priya (platform): yes, we'll add a startup warning in the quickstart image and a CI linter that scans Dockerfiles and build args for REDWOOD_ORG_KEY/ORG_* strings. infra-bot can create an issue for that.

infra-bot: created issue #923: Docker/CI scan for org-scoped token baking. Assigned to priya.

rafa (sdk): PR: https://git.redwood/sdks/pull/585 flips precedence and adds namespaced keyring API. Tests added. Leaving TODO to add rotate audit logs.

oliver (security): please also add a migration doc: how to clean old un-namespaced keyring entries and rotate tokens safely for devs who already cached keys.

lina (devex): I'll draft a short FAQ/upgrade note in the quickstart repo and update the sampleapp Dockerfile to `ENV REDWOOD_ORG_KEY=\"\"` so images don't carry org creds.

priya (platform): after PR merges, we'll roll a canary to quickstart and add an opt-in strict mode `REDWOOD_AUTH_STRICT=true` that rejects mismatched token/project combos.

rafa (sdk): +1. Thanks for catching this, lina. These edgecases are annoying for new users.

lina (devex): thanks team. closing once PR merged, Dockerfile updated, and migration note live. :thumbsup:
